claims.claim: Eustathius of Antioch was bishop of Antioch from approximately 324 to 327/330.
Eustathius was born at Side in Pamphylia and was first bishop of Beroea (modern Aleppo) before being transferred to Antioch around 323.
Eustathius died before 337, possibly in exile in Thrace.
Eustathius was one of the most prominent opponents of Arianism at the Council of Nicaea in 325.
Eustathius was deposed by a synod at Antioch in 327 or 330 and banished to Trajanopolis in Thrace by Emperor Constantine the Great due to intrigues led by the pro-Arian Bishop Eusebius of Caesarea.
The Commentary on Psalm 92 (Commentarius in Psalmum 92, CPG 3356) is among the works of Eustathius edited by J.H. Declerck.
Most of Eustathius's numerous dogmatic and exegetical treatises have been lost, with only fragments surviving.
The only complete work by Eustathius that survives is De Engastrimytho contra Origenem.
Eustathius's works survive indirectly through later sources such as catenae.
The Commentary on the Hexameron attributed to Eustathius in manuscripts is spurious and too late to be authentic.
Eustathius carried on an almost continuous literary warfare against the Arians from 325-330.
